questions.q: cis-But-2-ene reacts with mCPBA in CH₂Cl₂. The product is:
options: A 1:1 mixture of cis and trans epoxides
questions.explain: Epoxidation is a concerted syn addition, so alkene geometry is retained; the anti diol forms only if the epoxide is opened with water and acid.

questions.q: Which alkene reacts fastest with a peroxy acid?
questions.explain: The peroxy acid is the electrophile, so more alkyl groups on the C=C (more electron density) raise the rate; the tetrasubstituted alkene is fastest.

questions.q: Which reagent sequence converts cyclohexene into trans-cyclohexane-1,2-diol?
questions.explain: Water opens the epoxide from the face opposite the oxygen, giving the anti (trans) diol; Baeyer's reagent and OsO₄ give the syn diol.

questions.q: Which statement about the Prilezhaev reaction is correct?
options: It goes through a carbocation, so rearrangements are common
Electron-poor alkenes conjugated with C=O react fastest
Silver-catalysed O₂ oxidation is a general epoxidation method for all alkenes
The peroxy acid is converted into the corresponding carboxylic acid
questions.explain: The peroxy acid gives one O to the C=C and becomes RCOOH in a concerted butterfly step with no carbocation. Silver/O₂ works only for ethylene, and electron-poor alkenes react slowly.
